newsitem.title: CHILE: Pinochet celebrates 10th anniversary of ambush.
newsitem.headline: Pinochet celebrates 10th anniversary of ambush.

text.p: Former Chilean dictator Gen. Augusto Pinochet marked the tenth anniversary of a failed attempt against his life on Saturday by handing out medals to the widows of five bodyguards killed in the attack.
Armed left-wing opponents ambushed Pinochet's motorcade with bazookas and automatic gunfire on Sept. 7, 1986, as he returned from his weekend home in the Andes outside Santiago.

"I can still hear in my mind the echos of the mortal shots that were cowardly made against the presidential vehicle and its escort," Pinochet said at a ceremony in San Jose del Maipo near the site of the ambush.

Pinochet seized power in a military coup that overthrew Socialist Salvador Allende in 1973 and ruled Chile until he was forced to step down in 1990 after losing a plebiscite. But the 80-year-old army general is still commander-in-chief of the Chilean army.
Pinochet said the ambush was an attempt to draw the country into a civil war and reestablish a Marxist government.
"Chileans knew that they were at risk of returning to an ideology that did not want to accept its death in our country in 1973", he said, referring to the coup against Allende.
Twenty-four members of a leftist urban guerrilla group called the Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front carried out the ambush, though none are currently in jail.
Part of the group were caught but escaped from prison or were pardoned in exchange for leaving the country when democracy was restored under a civilian government in 1990.
